site.title: Hayden Huelskamp: working software demos
site.description: Six demonstration builds by Hayden Huelskamp: software for a law firm, a therapy practice, an accounting office, a government contractor, a home service company and a city transportation office. Demos, not client work.

projects.name: Law firm front office
projects.pitch: New inquiries answered, checked for conflicts and signed up as clients, without anyone at the firm retyping a thing.
try: On the client side, play the scripted inquiry called A conflict of interest.
Switch to the firm side and run the conflict check. It catches a current client who was given under a different name.
Sign an engagement letter as the client, then open the outbox to read what would have been sent.
projects.note: The intake assistant does not give legal advice, and says so when asked.
projects.alt: The client side of the law firm demo: a fictional firm's home page with a chat intake assistant

projects.name: Therapy practice scheduler
projects.pitch: A cancelled appointment fills itself: the time is offered to the waitlist, one person at a time, before anyone at the front desk picks up a phone.
try: Press Play the story for a tour of about two minutes, or book an appointment as a client.
On the practice side, have a client cancel and watch the time offered to the person who has waited longest.
Skip the demo clock ahead 20 minutes. The offer lapses and passes to the next person.
projects.note: Designed with HIPAA in mind. The demo is not HIPAA compliant or certified.
projects.alt: The client side of the therapy practice demo: booking an appointment with a fictional counseling practice

projects.name: Document AI extractor
projects.pitch: Invoices, receipts and W-9s are read by AI, checked by arithmetic, and held for a person whenever something does not add up. Every value shows where on the page it came from.
try: Open the plumber's invoice and click Subtotal. It lights up on the page, and the check shows the lines add up to $10 less.
Open the handwritten W-9, a phone photo. The tax ID is one digit short, and it was caught.
Approve the clean documents, then open the export.
projects.note: The AI readings were recorded ahead of time and are replayed. The arithmetic checks run live.
projects.alt: The document AI demo: an invoice beside the values read from it, each linked to its place on the page

projects.name: Government bid tracker
projects.pitch: New solicitations are read by AI, checked against what your company can take on, and turned into a checklist for the ones you bid. When an agency changes the rules midway, the change is shown before and after.
try: Open the rooftop unit job and click a checklist item. The sentence it came from lights up in the solicitation.
Skip to the next morning. An agency has moved a deadline and added a bond on a bid in progress.
Change the company profile and see which jobs come out differently before you save.
projects.note: The AI readings were recorded ahead of time and are replayed. Matching is done by written rules.
projects.alt: The government bid tracker demo: a solicitation with its fit against the company's profile and a bid checklist

projects.name: Service request and dispatch
projects.pitch: A service company's day on one board. Customer messages are read by AI, written rules suggest who to send and say why, and when a job runs long the board shows who will be kept waiting and proposes a fix.
try: Book a visit as a customer. Only times that can be kept are offered.
On the dispatcher's board, read a customer's message and who the rules would send, then send someone.
Skip ahead an hour. A job runs long and an emergency comes in. Accept the proposed reshuffle.
projects.note: The AI readings were recorded ahead of time and are replayed. No text is sent and no van is tracked.
projects.alt: The customer side of the service company demo: requesting a plumber from a fictional company

projects.name: Micromobility monitor
projects.pitch: For a city that permits shared scooters and bikes: check what each operator reports against its own data, judge the permit rules with the evidence kept, and bill from the trip records instead of taking the operator's word.
projects.tryTitle: Three things to look for in the screenshots
try: The public page: ride counts for finished months, with any count under 10 withheld and places shown only as coarse hexagons.
An operator's own page: where it stands on each permit rule, and nothing about any other operator.
An invoice worked out from the trip records, set beside the operator's own report, with the gap between them shown.
projects.note: Not hosted yet, so there is no live link: this one needs a database and a background worker running. The button opens its code and screenshots. The data is simulated, the operators are fictional, and it is not used by any city.
projects.alt: The public page of the micromobility monitor demo: monthly ride counts for three fictional scooter and bike operators
